content.title: What is File Handling?
content.description: File Handling in Java is the process of creating, reading, writing, updating, and deleting files stored on a computer. It enables applications to store data permanently instead of keeping it only in memory.

content.content: Normally, data stored in variables is lost when a program terminates. File handling allows Java applications to store information permanently in files so that it can be accessed later. Java provides classes such as File, FileReader, FileWriter, BufferedReader, and BufferedWriter to perform file operations.

content.title: Why Learn File Handling?
content.content: Almost every real-world application stores data in files, including configuration settings, logs, reports, CSV files, and text documents.
The File class in the java.io package represents files and directories. It provides methods for creating, deleting, renaming, and checking file properties.

content.title: Creating a File Object
content.code:
import java.io.File;

File file = new File("student.txt");

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: A File object represents the path to a file or directory. It does not automatically create the physical file.

content.content: The createNewFile() method creates a new file if it does not already exist.

content.title: Create File Example

content.content: The FileWriter class is used to write text data into a file. Existing content can be overwritten or appended depending on the constructor used.

content.title: Writing Data
Best Practice
content.content: Always close FileWriter after writing data to ensure all content is saved properly.
The FileReader class reads character data from a file, while BufferedReader provides faster and more convenient reading line by line.

items.question: createNewFile()
items.answer: Creates a new file if it does not already exist.

items.question: length()
items.answer: Returns the size of the file in bytes.

content.content: File operations may throw checked exceptions such as IOException or FileNotFoundException. These exceptions must be handled using try-catch blocks or declared using the throws keyword.

content.title: Notebook Storage
content.content: Writing information on paper preserves it even after you leave the classroom. Similarly, file handling stores data permanently so it remains available after the program stops.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Java interviews often include questions about the File class, FileReader vs FileWriter, BufferedReader, IOException, file creation, reading, writing, and best practices for closing resources.

items.question: Can a File object create a file automatically?
items.answer: No. A File object only represents a file path. Use createNewFile() to create the actual file.

items.question: Why should files be closed?
items.answer: Closing files releases system resources and ensures all buffered data is written.

items.question: Should file operations always handle IOException?
items.answer: Yes. Most file operations can throw checked exceptions that must be handled.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Use the File class to represent files, FileReader and FileWriter for reading and writing text, and always close resources after file operations.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: File handling provides permanent data storage.
The File class represents files and directories.
Always close file resources after use.
Handle IOException using try-catch or throws.
